newsitem.title: USA: Court upholds Virginia challenge of EPA car rule.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Virginia challenge of EPA car rule.

text.p: A federal appeals court Tuesday said the Environmental Protection Agency overstepped its authority when it ordered Virginia to adopt California's car emissions control programme to improve its air quality.

The U.S. Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia upheld Virginia's challenge, saying the EPA cannot require a particular measure to be part of a state's plan to meet federal air quality standards.

The case stemmed from the EPA's rule that Virginia and other northeastern states adopt California's programme to curb automobile pollution by using specially equipped cleaner conventional cars and phasing in electric cars.

The 12 northeastern states and the District of Columbia are members of the Ozone Transport Commission, which was formed under the Clean Air Act for the states to cooperate to try to deal with their serious smog problems.
The Northeast states' commission had petitioned the EPA to order the California emissions programme, but Virginia resisted.
Automakers also balked at the idea of building specific cars for the Northeast.
The EPA eventually adopted the California plan for the northeastern states only as a "backstop," and pinned its hopes on getting a national programme for cleaner cars.

"Today's ruling says that the use of cleaner cars to achieve air standards within the OTC (Ozone Transport Commission) is an option of individual states but can't be mandated for the OTC as a whole," the EPA said in a statement, which also called it a "narrow, technical ruling."
While the Virginia case was coming through the courts, the northeastern states have been negotiating with carmakers to offer a cleaner conventional gasoline-powered car nationwide.

The EPA has said this national plan would benefit the Northeast's air as much as California's stricter emissions control programme because there would be less pollution coming in from outside the region.

However that plan has stalled as the automakers tried to force Massachusetts and New York, which adopted California's plan, to drop their requirements that automakers make electric vehicles to sell in their states.
